Consider a message that is $7.5 \ast 10^6$ bits long to be sent from the source to the destination. (Assume header size is negligible relative to the entire message size). Suppose each link is $1.5$ Mbps. Focus on transmission delays only and assume all other delay components are negligible.

Suppose that the message is segmented into $5000$ packets, with each packet being $1500$ bits long. How long does it take to move the file from source host to destination host when message segmentation is used?

questions.qtext:
There are two nodes on a network $\text{C}$ and $\text{S. C}$ is the client and $\text{S}$ is the server. $\text{C}$ wants to connect to $\text{S}$ and send a message that is $35$ kilobytes long using TCP. Assume that a single packet can hold up to $2$ kilobytes of data and the headers are negligibly small. Processing time at both ends of the connection is negligible, but the latency in between node $\text{S}$ and node $\text{C}$ is $5$ ms. The link transmission rate is $10$ Megabits per second. Assume that control packets (SYN, ACK, etc) are very small and can be sent and received instantaneously.
Assuming $3$-way connection establishment and piggybacked ACKs, How many windows will be needed for the client to send the entire message?

questions.qtext:
Consider the following $\text{LL(1)}$ grammar.
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \text{S} \rightarrow \text{A} \\
& \text{A} \rightarrow \mathbf{a} \text{BE} \\
& \text{B} \rightarrow \mathbf{b} \text{CD} \\
& \text{C} \rightarrow \mathbf{c} \\
& \text{D} \rightarrow \mathbf{d} \\
& \text{E} \rightarrow \mathbf{e} \text{FG} \\
& \text{F} \rightarrow \mathbf{f} \\
& \text{G} \rightarrow \mathbf{g}
\end{aligned}
$$
In $\text{LL(1)}$ parsing, at each step in the parse the rule that must be chosen is uniquely determined by the current nonterminal and the next one lookahead symbol.
How many steps would the $\text{LL(1)}$ parser take to parse string $\textbf{abcdefg} ?$

Consider the following already augmented $\text{LR(1)}$ grammar -
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \text{S}^{\prime} \rightarrow \text{S} \\
& \text{S} \rightarrow \text{aAB} \mid \text {ecS } \mid \mathrm{aBb} \\
& \text{A} \rightarrow \text{aA} \mid \mathrm{a} \\
& \text{B} \rightarrow \text{cd} \mid \mathrm{Be}\mid \epsilon
\end{aligned}
$$
We have drawn start state of $\text{LR(1)}$ state automata as follow as-

How many states we will be needing (including start state) to parse $\text{aaaaee}.$ Your answer should include only necessary states and exclude all other states not needed to parse $\text{aaaaee}.$

questions.qtext:
If $\mathrm{A}$ is a set, let $|\mathrm{A}|$ denote the cardinality of set $\mathrm{A}$.

  • We say $\text{|B|}=|\text{A}|$ if and only if there exists a bijection from $\text{B}$ to $\text{A}$.
  • We say $|\mathrm{B}|<|\mathrm{A}|$ if and only if there exists an injection from $\mathrm{B}$ to $\mathrm{A}$ but there is no surjection from $\mathrm{B}$ to $\mathrm{A}$.

Which of the following is/are false?

options.text: If $\text{A}$ is a proper subset of $\text{B}$, then $\text{|A|}<|\text{B}|$.
The set of all infinite sequences of $0 \mathrm{s}$ and $1 \mathrm{s}$ is uncountable.
If $\text{A}$ is an uncountable set then $\text{|A|}=|\text{R}|. \;(\text{R}$ is set of all real numbers)
Set $\text{B}$ is infinitely countable if and only if there is a bijection $f: \text{N} \rightarrow \text{B}.\; ( \text{N}$ is set of all positive integers)
